To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the students of environmental studies, in contrast to general population, do not consider meat eating to be wrong, but they are aware of the ethical problems related to it.

the environmental studies students are more likely to be aware of the ethical issues related to meat consumption than the general population, and their attitudes are significantly influenced by the social circle they belong to, which is mostly comprised of fellow students and friends who share their views and values.

environmental studies graduate students do not regard meat eating as a wrong or undesirable thing in principle, yet they are well aware that there are many issues related to meat production and eating that make them feel bad about it.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the psychological dynamics of a group of people whose behavior and attitude toward meat eating is significantly influenced by their social circle, in contrast to general population where meat eating is a social norm.

the psychological processes involved when people who are aware of the ethical, environmental and health issues related to meat production, consumption and waste, still eat meat, and how they justify their meat eating.

the question of how people who are aware of the environmental and ethical issues related to meat, but who are also part of a group of people that is not necessarily vegetarian, cope with the cognitive dis-sonance induced by their awareness of these issues and their own meat eating.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the meat-eating behavior of the students is not only influenced by their own attitudes and values, but also by the social context and the social environment in which they live.

the students in this sample do not regard meat eating as a problem, but they are aware of the ethical, environmental, health and animal welfare issues related to it, and they are influenced in their behavior by their social circle.

the students of environmental studies are aware of the issues related to animal production and meat consumption, and that they are able to cope with the dissonance by adopting a more flexible attitude toward meat consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the meat-eating habits are not necessarily related to one's environmental awareness, as many studies show.
meat is not a simple issue, it is not a matter of a simple choice, but rather a matter of a complex set of values, attitudes, and social norms.
the meat-eating practices of the students in this study were influenced by their environmental values, their friends, and their social context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
meat eating is an important issue for the environmental movement and that there is need for more research on this issue, and on the attitudes and behavior of the people involved.
meat eating is a highly complex issue and that the dynamics of it cannot be understood without considering the social context in which the people live and the social norms they perceive.
the psychological dynamics related to meat eating may differ in different groups of people, which should be taken into account when designing campaigns to reduce meat consumption.
